headline: 7 Michigan deals, $369.1M raised — led by Cinnaire Fund for Housing Limited Partnership 45

top_deals.company: Cinnaire Fund for Housing Limited Partnership 45
top_deals.summary: Cinnaire Fund for Housing Limited Partnership 45, a Lansing-based private equity fund, disclosed a $308M raise; $307.1M sold to 17 investors.
LSPedia Inc., a Farmington Hill-based computers company, filed a $30.5M pooled fund interests offering under Rule 506(b); $30.5M sold to 3 investors.
Cambridge Avenue Partners II LLC, a Kalamazoo-based company, filed a $20M equity offering under Rule 506(b); $20M sold to 15 investors.
Milestone Capital Partners, Inc., a Troy-based company, filed a $11.5M debt offering under Rule 506(b); $11.5M sold to 3 investors.
Radar Midtown LLC, a Detroit-based residential real estate company, filed a $156.1K equity offering under Rule 504; $28.1K sold to 1 investor.

talking_points.text: Michigan issuers reported $369.1M sold across 5 Form D filings this week, up 593% vs. the prior 4-week average. The largest was LSPedia Inc. (Farmington Hill, Computers) targeting $30.5M. Good question to ask: are founders in technology favoring equity rounds over venture debt right now?

1 Michigan-based pooled fund filed Form Ds, reporting $307.1M raised so far — led by Cinnaire Fund for Housing Limited Partnership 45 (Private Equity Fund). A natural opener: what are LPs asking Michigan sponsors for in today's fundraising market?

The Donald A. Foss 2009 Remainder Trust and others reported a 19.8% stake in Credit Acceptance Corp (CACC) (Schedule 13D/A amendment 4). Schedule 13D filers can push for strategic change, so it's worth asking whether shareholders see a sale or restructuring on the table.
